what: File-by-file comparison of the BOXRR-23 processed corpus on AVALON and DESKTOP-C
why: Two machines held identical file and user counts and identical code_identity on every row, yet differed by 191 bytes in total. code_identity() hashes only model/*.py, and all four prepare_*.py sit at the repo root, so the digest cannot see a corpus difference at all. This is the measured instance behind the corpus-digest proposal.

inputs.path_normalisation: DESKTOP-C paths lead with './', AVALON's with 'BOXRR-23_Dataset/'. Both stripped. An assertion that 'PROVENANCE.md' resolves on BOTH sides gates the comparison - without it a wrong convention reports every file as simultaneously missing and extra, which is exactly what an earlier version of verify_corpus.py did on who_is_alyx.

result.independent_arithmetic: 42828352195 - 4832 - 784 = 42828346579, matching the coordinator's independently computed figure

conclusion: Size-identical across all 17,872 CSV files. The entire byte difference between the two machines is PROVENANCE.md, a per-machine file that legitimately differs.
explicitly_not_shown: Content equality at equal size. A size manifest cannot see content; sha256 over 42.8 GB was judged not worth ~2 h of disk on each end, because a size-level diff catches any plausible transfer or generation fault.
The correct sentence is 'size-identical across all 17,874 files, content unverified' - not 'identical'. Say the weaker sentence and it stays true.
consequence: A corpus digest should be computed over the CSV payload ONLY, excluding PROVENANCE.md and CITATION.txt. Including them makes every machine report a different corpus on day one, at which point somebody switches the guard off and it protects nothing.
